page: Microsoft Azure E64ds_v7 is an Edsv7-family virtual machine configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this server features 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8) for accelerated mathematical and matrix operations. The instance is bundled with 3780 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core processing and memory capabilities. The server achieved a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 89,771.17 and a strong multi-core stress-ng CPU performance score of 73,052.88. Memory performance is highlighted by a strong read-only large-block bandwidth of 332.26 GB/sec and a write large-block bandwidth of 128.16 GB/sec. In database operations, the instance demonstrated top-tier performance with a PassMark database score of 33,062.35 and a strong Redis SET throughput of 117.01 million operations per second. Single-threaded gzip compression reached a top-tier speed of 36.25 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput peaked at a top-tier 110.35 GB/sec. Large language model inference benchmarks show top-tier prompt processing speeds of 4,079.59 tokens per second for a small 135M model and 39.93 tokens per second for a large 70B model, though text generation speeds remain average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E64ds_v7 offers high resource density by combining a large 512.0 GB memory capacity with 3780 GB of local storage on a dedicated hardware class. This configuration minimizes the need for external storage attachments for high-throughput workloads, optimizing the resource-per-cost ratio. The server is highly suited for memory-intensive and database workloads, including large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, data warehousing, and high-throughput static web serving. Additionally, the presence of Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets makes it a viable option for CPU-based machine learning inference and vector-heavy mathematical computations.
